Prayer :

Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of In  praying this Court to issue a Writ of Mandamus forbearing the respondent  from dispossessing the Petitioner from his lands situate at S.F.No.56/3C  3B and 3G, 146/1D, 1E, 3C, 3B and 1B, Periyakottai Village, Udumalaipett  Taluk, Tiruppur District without serving the copy of the award made in  pursuance of the notification issued by the 4th respondent in his procee  in Na.Ka.No.1654/2018/A1/CU-209 dated 04.12.2018 under Section 3A of the  National Highways Act, 1956 and pass such further or other orders as thi  Honble Court may deem fit and proper in the circumstances of the case an  thus render justice.
For Petitioner : Ms.Afritha Fathima for M/s.Ajmal As

For Respondents : Mr.K.Govindarajan,
 Deputy Solicitor General of India fo  Mr.P.Karthik for R2  Mr.S.Ra.Ramachandran,
 Additional Government Pleader for R  ORDER Heard both sides.
2.The prayer in the writ petition is for protecting the petitioner from dispossession without serving copy of the award.
When the matter was taken https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis up for hearing, the copy of the award was served on the petitioner.
The limitation for the purpose of seeking enhancement of the compensation will be computed from 16.10.2023 only.
3.The learned Deputy Solicitor General of India appearing for the first respondent informs the court that the award amount has already been deposited in the appropriate account.
The petitioner is at liberty to seek arbitral remedy at the hands of the District Collector, Tiruppur for enhancement of compensation.
If such petition is filed before the third respondent, it shall be disposed of on merits and in accordance with law within a period of six months thereafter.
The stand of the respondents is that bank details have not been furnished.
It is controverted by the learned counsel for the petitioner.

Section 3H(4) of the National Highways Act, 1956 is as follows :
3H. Deposit and payment of amount.
